english.title: Cause / allow a child / vulnerable adult to suffer serious physical harm
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(1) and (8) of the Domestic Violence, Crime and Victims Act 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a member of the same household as and
having had frequent contact with a person
who was at that time a child/vulnerable adult
caused that person to suffer serious physical harm or
were / ought to have been aware
that there was a significant risk of serious physical harm
being caused to that person
by the unlawful act of a member of his / her household
which occurred in circumstances of the kind that you foresaw or
ought to have foreseen and failed to take such steps as you could reasonably have been expected to take
to protect him/her from that risk

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) On the 28th June 2022, the penalty for offences under this section was increased on indictment from a maximum of 10 years imprisonment to 14 years imprisonment by section 123 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. For the offence applying before that date, see H10501.
(ii) Section 5(2) provides that prosecution does not have to prove whether it was the defendant who committed the act or the person who failed to take steps to prevent it.
(iii) Section 5(3)(a) provides that if the accused was not the mother or father of the person who suffered serious harm then they MAY NOT be charged with this offence if they were under the age of 16 at the time of the act that caused the serious physical harm and section 5(3)(b) provides that for the purposes of subsection (1)(d)(ii) they could not have been expected to take any such step as is referred to there before attaining that age.

other.penalty:
Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
